trigger: a caller dispatching with a plugin name whose case differs from the catalogue's canonical spelling, against an agent that reports the canonical spelling
summary: AgentRegistry::ids_missing_plugin was called with the raw caller-supplied plugin string instead of classify()'s catalogue-resolved canonical spelling (classified->wire().plugin()) at both REST call sites (/api/command, legacy forward) -- case-sensitive matching against a case-insensitive classify() meant a differently-cased dispatch could be wrongly withheld as plugin-absent even though the agent has the plugin. Fixed in 117c6d727. Regression test added later (Gate 8 pass 5, see 3424-3511-br009-untested).

trigger: an operator or integrator reading docs/user-manual/metrics.md, mcp.md, rest-api.md, or upgrading.md for the new dispatch-outcome discrimination behavior with no updated entry
summary: Reconstructed summary (exact original wording not retained): docs-writer's Gate 2 pass identified required doc updates for the new unknown_plugin metric reason and plugin-inventory-staleness caveat, plus two stale in-code comments. Fixed in ca58ac578.

trigger: an operator or agentic caller hitting POST /api/instructions/{id}/execute's zero-agents-reached 503, which still collapsed all four causes into one generic body while /api/command and the legacy route already discriminated
summary: Gate 3 architect finding: /api/instructions/{id}/execute was not extended to the same 4-way split as the other two REST dispatch surfaces. Fixed in f9249a53b (discrimination logic) + 96c1343d2 (rest-api.md doc update) + a3897729e (a follow-up INFO-level overclaiming comment fix on containment_unreadable, same architect pass).

trigger: an agentic caller comparing MCP execute_instruction's status literal against REST's reason literal for the same underlying condition, or a MIXED partial dispatch (some reached, some withheld) on a route whose success body didn't surface the withheld counts
summary: Gate 4 convergent finding (independently raised by unhappy-path's Finding 1, consistency-auditor's Finding 2/UP-2, and noted in the changelog review as Finding 3): MCP's zero-reach status literal was "targets_quarantined" where REST used "quarantined" (no parity), and a mixed-cause partial dispatch on /api/command's success path was silently invisible. Fixed in aa9358fe8: MCP renamed to "quarantined"; /api/command's success body gained withheld_quarantined/withheld_unknown_plugin.

adjudicated_by: compliance-officer (independent fresh-agent re-derivation, no context from the original reporter's framing)
adjudication_rationale: The original finding's core comparison was factually wrong: the cited 'sibling reasons' (scope_empty/agent_ids_type/destructive_untargeted) are PRE-DISPATCH request-shape validation denials (400s, kTargetingShapeReasons/kRouteRejectReasons, a different metric family per dispatch_target_shape.hpp's own doc comment) fired BEFORE target resolution, not POST-DISPATCH outcome reasons like unknown_plugin (503s, fired inside the same sent==0 block as containment_unreadable/quarantined/generic-offline). The TRUE same-phase siblings are containment_unreadable and the generic offline catch-all -- both of which ALSO get zero audit rows in server.cpp's sent==0 block, pre-existing and unchanged by this PR. dispatch_target_shape.hpp's own in-tree doc comment (lines ~179-188) already states the unknown_plugin no-audit-row rationale. docs/user-manual/audit-log.md line 3 ('Yuzu records every operator action as a structured audit event') is opening framing prose, not a per-branch enumerated guarantee, and was already not literally true for containment_unreadable before this PR. No MUST/never/catastrophic-if-violated clause in CLAUDE.md, either routed-concerns file, or any accepted ADR requires an audit row for every dispatch-outcome branch -- no policy floor applies. Independently re-derived by a FRESH compliance-officer agent instance (no shared context with the original reporter or the orchestrating session's framing), given only the phase-distinction evidence and the containment_unreadable precedent, and asked explicitly to hold HIGH if the evidence did not change its mind. It did not hold HIGH; it landed at 'not HIGH/blocking... At most LOW/advisory' and found an even stronger precedent independently (the generic-offline branch also gets zero audit rows).
refuted_by: Direct trace of server.cpp's sent==0 block (all three REST-family routes) confirms containment_unreadable and the generic catch-all get NO audit_log call either -- only quarantined does, via separate pre-existing helpers called before response-building. Confirmed independently by a second, fresh compliance-officer instance.
refuted_by_reporter: compliance-officer (independent re-derivation instance, Gate 8 pass, not the original reporter)
trigger: an auditor asking 'show me evidence a plugin-absence withholding was reviewed' for the unknown_plugin dispatch-outcome reason specifically
summary: Original Gate 6 report: HIGH/blocking, claiming unknown_plugin's counter-and-warn-only design (no audit row) was inconsistent with sibling reasons that DO get audit rows 'from the same call sites'. DOWNGRADED after independent adjudication (see adjudication_rationale) to MEDIUM/non-blocking -- unknown_plugin's no-audit-row posture matches its true same-phase siblings (containment_unreadable, generic-offline), both pre-existing and unaudited. Narrow valid piece extracted and fixed regardless: mcp_server.cpp's mcp_audit call hardcoded a 'no_agents_reached' detail string regardless of which of the four zero_status branches actually fired -- now threads zero_status. Fixed in ff20d231e.

trigger: a misconfigured automation retrying against an absent plugin, incrementing yuzu_server_dispatch_target_rejected_total{reason="unknown_plugin"} past the >3/15m threshold with no exclusion, the same false-positive shape the quarantined exclusion already exists to avoid
summary: YuzuDispatchTargetRejected's expression excluded reason="quarantined" only; unknown_plugin was not excluded and would page ops on an ordinary caller mistake. Fixed in ff20d231e: reason!~"quarantined|unknown_plugin", with promtool CASE 61b/62b added mirroring the existing CASE 61/62 pair (Gate 8 pass 5, test-*.yml commit).

trigger: an operator using the dashboard exec console (POST /api/dashboard/execute) during a containment or quarantine incident, seeing an unconditional 'No agents connected. Cannot dispatch command.' message that misdirects toward a connectivity fix
summary: This is a fourth dispatch surface (dashboard exec console) entirely unaddressed by the original implementation: it captured the same ConfinedDispatchOutcome but read only .command_id/.sent, so a containment/quarantine/plugin-absence zero-reach dispatch showed the same generic connectivity message pre-existing before this PR -- a genuine regression vs. the REST-family surfaces this PR fixed, since the operator console is the primary human-facing surface. Fixed in ff20d231e: reads .containment_unreadable/.denied_quarantined_count/.unknown_plugin_count to pick the right message.

summary: rest-api.md claimed the dashboard toast mirrors /api/command's success-body withheld fields -- false, dashboard_ui.cpp never calls /api/command at all (it's a separate HTML-fragment handler). Fixed in ff20d231e's doc pass.

trigger: a scope/broadcast dispatch that partially succeeds (some targets withheld) on MCP execute_instruction, the legacy forward route, or /api/instructions/{id}/execute -- none of whose success paths surface withheld counts, unlike /api/command's success body
summary: Only /api/command's success body gained withheld_quarantined/withheld_unknown_plugin this PR; the other three surfaces' success paths carry neither field, so a partial-withheld dispatch is invisible to those callers. Not fixed in this PR (would require an MCP output-schema widening that invalidates prior reviewers' 'success branch unchanged' sign-off, a deliberate scope boundary) -- filed as https://github.com/Tr3kkR/Yuzu/issues/3930, documented in the changelog fragment (831013ab5).

Documented via a doc note added in 831013ab5 rather than a rename, since renaming either would be a breaking change for no correctness gain.
